economic-model-rows-modules-data-and-fun.text: Economic model rows: modules, data and functions of slices five to ten.

This page owns the new or changed rows of the economic slices, in the same three layers as the modules, data and functions pages of the protected rejection rule, for the economics plan and the design. It contains no bodies and no proofs. The rows here say what each slice owns; the exact signatures of a slice are added to this page by the ticket owner before that slice is dispatched, so that no writer chooses a name that another slice, the transport or the paper depends on.

story.text: As the writer given an economic slice, I read the rows of that slice and nothing I have to guess, so that the model, the transport and the paper name every amount, parameter and statement the same way.

modules.text: The new module is imported by the root module so the axiom gate and the audit report walk it. The model checker refuses a change to the imports of Singular.Model beyond the naming layer's, which is why the vocabulary types sit in the model file and only functions over them sit in Singular.Economics.

data.text: Validation and invariants. An old input without these fields reads as the defaults, so every existing question, scenario and corpus row means what it meant and a fold's question is exactly what it was. Every step preserves the three parameters exactly as it preserves the pins. A request is pending only if a booking produced it. The supply of a token kind counts the tokens held at the application's custody and the tokens held by pending requests until the fold burns them.

functions-named-here-signed-before-dispa.text: A statement is declared where the plan puts it, never beside its definition in Economics, so the axiom gate and the register cover it.

slice-six-as-built.text: The registration booking is modelled by RegistrationRequest (with carrierAda, the declared carrier allocation), exactContents, registrationBookingRefusal, the request pool, book, World and WorldReachable, in Singular/Economics/, with the statements in Singular/Statements/Booking.lean. The syntax tag's identity is Config.syntaxTag = (registryId, 1) beside Config.stateToken = (registryId, 0): an abstraction, with no new configuration pin, whose relation to real policy identities and asset names is left to the correspondence work. The application tag keeps the historical Approval type and approvalAssetName. Booking observations separate syntax tags, application tags and other assets, so later slices that burn tags read the same separation.

slice-seven-as-built.text: The termination booking is modelled in Singular/Model/Termination.lean and Singular/Economics/Termination.lean (terminationBookingRefusal, terminationExactContents, terminationCustody) and extends the world in Singular/Economics/World.lean (bookTermination, bookTerminations, worldSingularSupply, WorldReachable). The singular tag leaves the application's custody into the pending request; the key's leaf stays active; the supply law counts custody plus pending terminations, so the registry component of a world with a pending termination is not consistent in the registry-level sense and the world-level law replaces it for worlds. A transaction is accepted or refused as a whole. Statements, in Singular/Statements/: at_most_one_pending_termination, world_supply_sync, termination_request_carries_genuine_token, and the supporting termination_booking_has_exact_contents.

What slice ten must follow: the termination fold consumes the pending request and its carried singular tag, burns the singular tag and the trie-ready tag (a termination holds no application tag from slice seven-b on), makes the leaf terminal, leaves no pending termination for it, extends WorldReachable with the real transition and reproves the world law and provenance for the remaining requests; the donation is the held lovelace minus the declared tip; a termination has neither booked time nor refund address, so its fold adds no window; rejection and retraction never consume a termination; reference uniqueness is shared across both pools; the trie-ready tags across both pools equal the pending requests, and the application tags held by pending registrations equal their number with exactly one each (the planned tag_supplies_equal_pending; no total supply of the application tag is claimed, because minting it is the application's own judgement). Slice seven-b restates this slice's termination declarations: the application tag is removed and the syntax tag is renamed the trie-ready tag.

slices-eight-a-seven-b-and-seven-c-plann.text: Slices eight-a, seven-b and seven-c: planned rows (15 October 2026).
Rows only; the exact signatures of each slice are added to this page by the ticket owner before that slice is dispatched.

slice-seven-b-as-built.text: The booking declarations built under the name syntax tag take the trie-ready names (Config.trieReadyTag, the booking contents' trieReadyTags, the two bookings' trieReadyTagsMinted, the refusal forged-trie-ready-tag); main's names are untouched. A termination holds, mints and checks no application tag, and one that holds an application tag is refused dirty-request. Each request carries one nonce (default zero, omitted from the written form at zero). The application tag's name commits to the registration payload and the nonce, the trie-ready tag's name to the operation and the nonce, in a canonical encoding of complete natural numbers with a stand-in hash; no injectivity is assumed. Trie-ready names are encoded as the commitment plus one, so that the name zero stays the state token's under the registry's policy, and the separation is proved for every commitment value. The statements in Singular/Statements/Booking.lean and Termination.lean, all from the standard axioms: booked_request_has_exact_contents, termination_booking_has_exact_contents (restated), booked_request_tags_commit_to_own_fields, booked_termination_tag_commits_to_own_operation and trie_ready_tag_is_not_state_token (new), beside the six statements of slices six and seven that keep their text. The booking corpus holds 48 registration rows and 36 termination rows, with exact-reason controls for foreign fields, operation kind, nonce, values that differ by 256, state-token collisions, preconditions, multiplicity and custody. Slice ten must burn one trie-ready tag per request and one application tag per registration only, and the planned tag_supplies_equal_pending counts application tags over registrations only. The hash is a stand-in: the correspondence of the commitments to the real policies and asset names is left to the correspondence work.

slice-eight-as-built.text: The ruled rejection is a separate economic judgement in Singular/Economics/ (the observed economic transaction beside Tx, the observation of unspent outputs with their pending contents, rejectionAccepted, the request address's spending arms and the world constructor for an admitted rejection), with its statements in Singular/Statements/RejectionState.lean and RejectionProtection.lean. It reads the registry state output by reference (the exact state token, the inline configuration and the current root are read from the actual unspent output, never from an input's claim), spends no state output, takes distinct pending registrations out of the pending pool together or not at all, and burns each member's trie-ready and application tags with the quantities summed by asset identity, collisions included. A live registration, an early expiry, a repeated input, a termination or a tag carried out alive refuses the whole batch. The seven statements, all from the standard axioms: rejection_leaves_registry_untouched, rejection_requires_referenced_state, rejection_cannot_invalidate_fold, rejection_batch_members_distinct, sweep_leaves_pool_untouched, live_request_not_rejected and termination_unrejectable (statements 2, 5, 3, the two supporting ones, 4 and 8). The earlier statements of slices six and seven keep their text and gained proof cases for the new world constructor. The evidence-bound rejection of slices two and three, its statements and the driver's old fold-with-rejection question are untouched and answer exactly as before; seven named adapters in a legacy module identify the superseded path (the state-spending rejection the deployed validators still follow) by definitional equality, and no statement of this slice is proved about it. The driver is named, not rewired, because rewiring edits main's declarations and the shared transport. The corpus holds 41 controls. Refunds are slice nine's and the economic folds slice ten's; the live rows that still follow the superseded path are slice eight-c's.

slice-ten-as-built.text: The economic fold is a separate judgement in Singular/Economics/ (Fold.lean, FoldProjection.lean and their siblings) beside the ruled rejection and retraction, over the observed economic transaction and the unspent set. It consumes pending requests by reference in spending-input order with their full observed contents, spends the actual state output (found by its token and checked for identity, quantity, inline configuration and current root) and continues it with the original value and the registry result. A registration is admitted only inside its own window with a non-empty interval whose lower bound is its booked time; a termination has no window, no clock and no application tag; an empty batch or a refused member refuses the whole transaction. The registry's transition is the unchanged batch law, applied through an explicit projection that restores each pending termination's retained custody holding and supplies syntactic legacy approvals for that interface only; its correspondence to the legacy result is a proved lemma about the registry component, not equality of admissions. Outputs and inputs are classified by what they hold (state, carrier, ordinary), never by address; the destination output holds the minted singular tag, the booked datum and exactly the declared carrier, and ordinary change is a separate output even at the same address. The donation is exactly the registration costs plus each termination's held minus tip; the ledger fee is funded by ordinary inputs; the world gains a default-zero cumulative treasury. The six public statements, all from the standard axioms: fold_donates_registration_cost, only_booked_terminations_fold, booked_termination_foldable, processors_take_at_most_the_tips, fold_routes_every_amount (which derives the gross equation: ordinary outputs plus the fee equal ordinary inputs plus the consumed tips) and tag_supplies_equal_pending (the trie-ready tags in the world equal the pending requests; the application tags held by pending registrations equal their number, one each; no total supply outside Singular). The availability statement constructs the coherent unspent set from the reachable world and the supplied funding, with the funding, the fee at most the declared tip and the folder's willingness as visible hypotheses; it is model transaction existence, not inclusion, a builder or fee funding in the ledger. The statements about reward are gross allocations, not total wealth at a shared address. Five earlier proofs gained a fold case with their statement text unchanged. The corpus holds 45 fold controls (nine accepted, 36 refused). The 1.18.0 entry of the constitution now carries the economic rows and the "Ruled economic translation" section, and says the legacy rows are superseded by the ruled rows while the live rows stay unmet.

slice-nine-as-built.text: The refund obligations and the economic retraction are separate judgements in Singular/Economics/ beside the ruled rejection (Refunds.lean, Rejection.lean, Retraction.lean, World.lean), with the observed refund read from the economic output's address and lovelace and no second payment field. An accepted rejection owes each refund address the sum, over the distinct rejected requests it appears in, of the held lovelace minus the declared tip (the registration cost and the carrier ada are inside that sum; the tip is the processor's), and refuses the whole batch with reject-refund-short when the observed lovelace at an address falls short. An accepted retraction spends exactly one observed pending registration, signed by its refund address, with a non-empty validity interval wholly inside the booked reclaim window, reads and spends no state output, burns both request tags in the same transaction with none retained, leaves the state and singular supply unchanged, returns at least the whole held amount to the refund address and removes the request from the pending pool; its world constructor is added to WorldReachable and the five earlier induction proofs gained cases without a change of statement text. The four public statements, all from the standard axioms, are rejection_refund_floor, retraction_refund_floor, registration_cost_returned_on_exit and refunds_sum_per_address (Statements/Refunds.lean), supported by eleven helper lemmas in Lemmas/Refunds.lean, appended uncovered. The statements about an address are floors on all lovelace received at that address: a payment to the same address for another purpose counts, and the model cannot tell a refund output from another output by its purpose. Exact processor take, treasury routing, full balance, the ledger minimum and the economic fold are slice ten's. The corpus holds 31 controls in Main/Refunds.lean (six accepted, 25 refused).

slice-eight-c-as-built.text: The five live rows that follow the superseded rejection (the deployed validators and builders still spend the registry state output inside the fold) are published as unmet by ruling with the reason "implementation follows the superseded rule; the ruled rule is not implemented": reject-after-window, reject-before-deadline-consumer-requirement, request-value-and-refund-routing, reject-and-retract-refund-controls and reject-inside-processing-and-retraction-windows. Their names, programs, expected comparisons, history and bindings are kept; the earlier consumer requirements of the processing-window and refund-routing rows stand beside the new ruling; each place a row's standing is stated carries a dated note. The tripwire is the slice three mechanism applied again: the dedicated early-rejection row expects the chain to accept the two untampered rejections that spend the state output, the hosted jobs assert the exact debt sets and verdicts, and on the day the deployed validators refuse such a rejection the expectation stops matching and the session goes red naming the row, the step, the expected and observed outcome and saying that the real outcome changed and the ruled rule may be deployed, never that it is; a seeded control proves the red, and a setup, node or crash failure is a different failure that the diagnostic does not use. The running book renders the unmet chapters as unmet and keeps its debt exit. The reader-facing pages carry dated qualifications; no validator, builder, command, Lean declaration, driver or transport changed. New Lean proofs alone cannot remove these standings: the validators and builders must meet the ruled behavior with complete live evidence first, and the changed outcome then triggers the tripwire and a reviewed replacement of the legacy expectations.

slice-seven-c-as-built.text: The configuration carries one tip number, minimumTip, always written and read under the existing key maxFee; the key minimumTip of slice five is gone from the written form, and the registration cost and booking width keep their omit-at-zero rule. The booking judgements of slices six and seven read the one field. The tip-cover predicate (lovelaceCoversTip), its hypothesis and conjunct in insert_active_transaction_row and update_terminal_transaction_row (the hypothesis was an echo of the conjunct, so both statements now hold for every request input lovelace), the four transaction-row annotation fields of the corpora, the exporter's guard and the two scenario rows about the old fee pin are retired; parameters_preserved_by_fold and parameters_preserved_by_batch conclude equality of the one tip number, and every restated or replaced identity is appended, uncovered, to the restatement table. The transaction baseline lost exactly eight top-level annotation lines and no other byte, and its compatibility check names the two retired fields as an explicit, scoped exception (4347 planted scalar mutations were refused by the real comparator). The protected coverage base record moved by exactly two identity strings, as it did for the first restatement of these two statements; two conformance modules that bind a restated theorem digest directly (Registration.hs, Retirement.hs) changed only their digest strings, and the marked appendix binding lost the retired conjunct. A repository search by the four old digests found twelve hits, all dispositioned. The classified consumers are 996 matching lines in 65 tracked files; no live conformance row or published row changes its expected result from this slice alone, and none is newly marked unmet, because the emitted configuration keeps the historical wire key, the general control wrong-fee still perturbs the compared maxFee observation, and the chain datum, off-chain readers, validators, builders and command line are untouched. The driver protocol version stays 7. Slice ten states that the processor takes exactly the declared tip; slice eight-c owns the tripwire and the publication of implementation gaps as unmet by ruling.

slice-eight-a-as-built.text: The fold model moved without a change of meaning. Singular/Model.lean, Lemmas.lean and Statements.lean are facades that import their children, so every import path works. The model's fold declarations live in Singular/Model/ (Admission, Exits, Fold, Payments, Routing), the lemmas that unfold them in Singular/Lemmas/ (Batch, State, Step, Transactions, beside the existing Assets, Payments and Retraction), and the fold statements in Singular/Statements/ by the property each group proves (Admission, Batch, Delivery, ExitPayments, Inversions, Preservation, RegistrationTransaction, TerminationTransaction, and the rejection group added to the existing Rejection). Twenty-nine complete moved source spans in eighteen groups equal their text at the base, and the fold lane's declarations equal their text on main. The 2202 non-internal declaration names are the same before and after (Lean's own classification; four compiler-generated auxiliary names disappeared and eleven appeared, all published as the internal difference), every statement keeps its AXIOMS line and digest, and the corpora of scenarios, the transaction baseline and the protocol version are byte-identical. The two mutant checkers (issue 566) are unchanged; the new places of the declarations they mutate are listed for that issue's owner. Slices seven-c, eight and ten add to these modules and never back to the facades.

slice-eleven-planned-rows-16-october-202.text: Rows only; the exact signatures of the slice are added to this page by the ticket owner when the slice is accepted, from its statement list.

slice-eleven-as-built.text: The accepted retraction (Singular/Economics/Retraction.lean, with its funding classification in Economics/RetractionFunding.lean) selects the one consumed pending registration by reference (a consumed pending termination is refused as retract-registration-only) and admits further inputs only as ordinary funding: no state token, no trie-ready, application or singular tag, neither the request role nor the state role, no request datum. Spending inputs are present, distinct and disjoint from the reference inputs. Ordinary funding and change are lovelace only: an unrelated native asset in a spent or produced value is refused as retract-foreign-asset, checked before the registry-supply guard, as the fold refuses it. The refund address signs, the whole interval lies inside the booked reclaim window, no state output is read or spent, both tags burn, the registry supply is unchanged and the request leaves the pending pool. The refund address receives at least everything the request held except the two tags, by actual output lovelace; the transaction balances, donates nothing, leaves the world treasury unchanged and pays its fee from ordinary funding. Change may go to any address: the model has no wallet-ownership or output-purpose observation, so another-address change cannot be told from a payment to a third party, and neither can take the request's cost or tip.

Two statements are new: Singular.Statements.retraction_pays_only_the_refund_and_the_fee (over accepted retractions in reachable worlds: zero donation, the refund floor, the fee at most the ordinary funding, full balance, and the value paid to any other address at most the ordinary funding left after the fee, derived from conservation and not guarded in admission) and Singular.Statements.pending_registration_can_be_retracted (a coherent unspent set and a balanced accepted retraction exist for a reachable pending registration, a nonempty interval inside its reclaim window, a signing refund address and ordinary funding that covers the fee; it claims no wallet funds, ledger minimum, inclusion or builder). Both print standard axioms only. Two earlier statements restate their singleton input clause as "the pending registration is among the inputs": retraction_refund_floor and registration_cost_returned_on_exit (same names, new text), with the helper RefundProof.retraction_request; the historical identities stay in the restatement record and the new ones start uncovered. Twenty new theorem identities (two public, eighteen helpers) are appended uncovered; the coverage inventory is 298 obligations, 118 manifest-bound and 180 unclassified, and its completion check exits one by design. The 43 controls (the funded retraction with a positive fee, the fee one lovelace beyond the funding, change and funding at other addresses, each non-ordinary input, the foreign-asset funding and change, a diverted tip, and the slice nine refusals) run against the actual judgement. The constitution's 1.18.0 entry and its retraction and availability rows state the ordinary funding and the fee. Rejection, the economic fold, the legacy retraction and the driver are unchanged; the live rows that follow the superseded retraction stay unmet.

slice-five-signed-rows.text: Names and shapes the writer keeps; anything not stated is the writer's to choose, and a name that another slice or the paper depends on is stated here.
The driver protocol version moves only if a declared question's written form changes; with every new field omitted at its default none does, and the writer says so in the first checkpoint.
